basis.claim: The comparable Deere pack carries no thesis, management, peer or model evidence at all, so no side-by-side judgment of its fundamentals is possible from these packs.
Both names' fit scores are ABSENT rather than low, so factor fit cannot separate them.
Boeing's own evidence shows a genuine turn: revenues of $89,463 million with $4,281 million of operating earnings in 2025 versus a $10,707 million loss in 2024, and a $682,207 million backlog.
That turn is flattered by a one-off $9,566 million Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture gain, while free cash flow remained negative at -$1,877 million and adjusted EBITDA was -$3,920 million.
Boeing still carries negative book value per share, $54.1 billion of debt at the lowest investment-grade ratings, and a suspended dividend.
The thesis rests on delivery ramp and certification milestones that remain FAA-dependent and subject to 777X and 737-7/-10 slippage risk.

sa_candidates.reason: the 11 defs of sa_rest_fetch.py minus the 6 non-endpoint helpers leave 5 endpoints (symbol, news, report, analysis, article) and none returns a comparables list; and build_session() needs the parked session bundle from Secrets Manager 'seeking-alpha/session' (the CRO's session vault), so the call is not reachable under this session's egress -- recorded as an INPUT candidate that does not exist, never as the rule

notes.Communication Services: same straddle as Consumer Discretionary: 'Media and Publishing Services' is GICS Communication Services, 'Hospitality Services' is not; rung 4 separates them
notes.Consumer Discretionary: scanner 'Consumer Services' holds BOTH the GICS Consumer Discretionary half ('Hospitality Services') and the GICS Communication Services half ('Media and Publishing Services'), so both GICS sectors claim it at rung 1 and rung 4 (industryGroup) separates them
notes.Industrials: scanner 'Business Services' (47 rows) is carved out of what GICS calls Industrials; rung 4 (industryGroup) separates 'Business Services' from 'Industrial Manufacturing' / 'Industrial Services' again
notes.Real Estate: the scanner has no Real Estate SECTOR -- it carries industryGroup 'Real Estate' (130 rows) inside sector 'Finance'

sector_map.residue_reason: no GICS sector claims 'Non-Corporate' (1 row, industryGroup 'Financially Operative Institutions') -- it is unreachable from a model-block subject and stays a scanner-only sector

subject.cross_vintage_caveat: the subject's scalars carry the model block's own vintage (2026-09-19T07:53:20Z); every candidate carries the scanner's asOf -- the band is graded ACROSS those two vintages and neither is re-dated
subject.fx_basis: USD; model block CUR_MKT_CAP in full currency units divided by 1e+06, bloomberg-dapi vintage 2026-09-19T07:53:20Z; no FX rate applied and none needed
subject.market_cap_unit_note: Current market capitalization, full currency units (not millions).
subject.name: BOEING CO/THE
subject.size_band_basis: COMPARABLE: cap is USD millions at model-block vintage 2026-09-19T07:53:20Z against a scanner-sourced candidate band -- SAME CURRENCY, cross-vintage caveat named separately above

peers.test: comparable = the deepest of four lexicographic rungs the candidate reaches: (1) same SECTOR (scanner UniverseDataRow.sector; a model-block subject's GICS_SECTOR_NAME is mapped into that vocabulary by GICS11_TO_SCANNER13_v1), then (2) a SIZE BAND of 0.2x-5.0x of the subject's market cap (UniverseDataRow.mktVal in USD millions; a model-block subject's CUR_MKT_CAP divided by 1e6), then (3) same COUNTRY (UniverseDataRow.country; CNTRY_OF_DOMICILE mapped by ISO3166A2_TO_SCANNER_COUNTRY_v1), then (4) same SUBSECTOR (UniverseDataRow.industryGroup); ties inside the deepest rung broken by the numeric similarity |log(candidate cap / subject cap)|. Similarity of business and scale, never valuation.
